clue.text: Stern guard, with thick back, but weak in the end.

indicators.note: in the end places the word for weak after the other piece, at the close
back tells us to read the word for thick from right to left

parts.note: thick means fat, as in a fat volume
weak means frail

explanation.surface: A rear protector, sturdy behind but feeble at its far end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for thick and 'in the end' sends the word for weak to the close. A taffrail is the rail round a ship's stern, which 'Stern guard' disguises.
explanation.definitionFit: A taffrail is the handrail running round the stern of a ship, guarding the poop deck.

clue.text: Choice between appropriation and benefaction.

parts.note: an offer one must accept wholly or decline, read as a choice between grabbing something and bequeathing it

explanation.walkthrough: Taking something is appropriation; leaving it to someone in a will is benefaction, so the phrase literally offers those two.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a non-negotiable offer: accept as stated or refuse.

clue.text: One side of the east, in reality.

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for east goes inside the word for reality

parts.note: reality means fact, the truth of things
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E inside FACT, between the A and the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one face or aspect of a cut gem or of a problem.

clue.text: Stop to take on water after a break

indicators.note: after places the word for water following the word for a break

parts.note: a break is a rest
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Halting to drink water after a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists water first, but 'after' puts it second; 'to take on' is only link.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or check, a synonym of stop as a verb.

clue.text: Senseless, in truth, to train an elk to a diet of mousse!

indicators.note: in truth here signals that the answer truly sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: Trying to put an elk on a diet of mousse would be truly pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across tRAIN AN Elk; the mousse diet is just colour for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or devoid of sense, a direct synonym.

clue.text: More venturesome; evidently not a case of stony silence!

indicators.note: evidently not, combined with silence, means the thing is spoken rather than kept quiet
a case of not silence is one where something is said out loud

parts.note: a case of stony matter, a big rock, is a boulder

explanation.surface: Braver, apparently, than someone keeping stony silence.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, a big rock and the comparative of bold are identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolder means more daring, readier to take risks.

clue.text: Alight from a train of explosives, perhaps.

definitions.text: Alight from a train of explosives, perhaps.

parts.words: Alight from a train of explosives, perhaps.
parts.note: not stepping off a railway train, but set burning by a lit fuse or chain of explosives

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests getting off a train; 'alight' is really the adjective meaning burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Alight as an adjective means burning, ablaze.

clue.text: Substantially provided for in case cited — Oh, dry up!

indicators.note: the substance of the answer is supplied in the next words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer told to shut up after quoting precedent.
explanation.walkthrough: CASE CITED rearranged gives the nine letters exactly; 'Oh' is mere exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: To desiccate is to remove moisture, to dry thoroughly.

clue.text: A King's Messenger wouldn't normally serve on it; or would he?

definitions.text: A King's Messenger wouldn't normally serve on it; or would he?

parts.words: A King's Messenger wouldn't normally serve on it; or would he?
parts.note: a formal government inquiry panel, though a royal courier also carries a mandate from the sovereign

explanation.walkthrough: A King's Messenger is a British diplomatic courier; he holds a commission from the monarch, hence the teasing 'or would he?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Royal Commission is a formal public inquiry set up by the Crown in Britain.

clue.text: To make a sudden arrest in a dangerous traffic situation?

definitions.text: To make a sudden arrest in a dangerous traffic situation?

parts.words: To make a sudden arrest in a dangerous traffic situation?
parts.note: arrest here means halting, not a police detention, as a driver brakes suddenly

explanation.walkthrough: 'arrest' suggests police; it means stopping motion.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt abruptly and completely is the meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: Preliminary engagement to go on with, to boot.

definitions.text: Preliminary engagement to go on with, to boot.

parts.words: Preliminary engagement to go on with, to boot.
parts.note: the first action that sets something going, done literally with a boot, as on a motorbike

explanation.walkthrough: 'to boot' usually means 'as well'; here it is the foot that kicks the pedal to start a motorcycle engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick-start is an initial impetus, originally the pedal kicked to fire a motorcycle engine.

clue.text: Kind of stuffy, but not so strong as it was — smelly, though.

indicators.note: kind of suggests a variant form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not so, with as it was, means a letter has been taken away from the word

parts.note: F (forte) is the musical abbreviation for strong or loud

explanation.surface: A stuffy room, less powerful than before but still smelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one F from STUFFY to leave STUFY, then 'Kind of' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusty describes a stale, musty odour.

clue.text: Engrave in faint erosive lines.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: Carving weak eroded lines into stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across faINT ERosive. 'Engrave' read as en-grave, put in a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, to place in a grave.

clue.text: Known as the result of a trial.

definitions.text: Known as the result of a trial.

parts.words: Known as the result of a trial.
parts.note: a trial here is an experiment, not a court case, and knowledge gained from it

explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' suggests court; it means an experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Empirical knowledge comes from observation and experiment rather than theory.

clue.text: Dungeons built to see in different circumstances.

indicators.note: different circumstances means the letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: Cells constructed to be viewed under various conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret dungeon reached only by a trapdoor above.

clue.text: Bumble bug which produces just inflated stick-jaw.

indicators.note: which produces means the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An insect that creates nothing but puffed-up chewing sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Stick-jaw is old British slang for a chewy sweet that glues the jaws; the anagram of BUMBLE BUG is exact.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubble gum is chewing gum that can be blown into bubbles.

clue.text: Very searching, despite the crudity.

parts.note: tho is an informal short form of though, meaning despite that
rough means crude, unpolished

explanation.surface: Probing deeply even though the manner is crude.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough inquiry is exhaustive and very searching.

clue.text: Something to ring the Head about?

definitions.text: Something to ring the Head about?

parts.words: Something to ring the Head about?
parts.note: not telephoning the headmaster but a circle of light encircling a saint's head

explanation.walkthrough: 'ring the Head' suggests calling a headteacher; ring means encircle.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a disc or ring of light round a holy figure's head.

clue.text: Even a lobster so treated can become fit to be kept.

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are processed into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Even a lobster, if cured properly, can be preserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Storable means able to be stored or kept.

clue.text: The ups and downs of court procedure.

definitions.text: The ups and downs of court procedure.

parts.words: The ups and downs of court procedure.
parts.note: a tennis court, where high shots rise and drop, not a law court

explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests law; it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A lob is a high arching shot in tennis that goes up and comes down.

clue.text: The sort of guard to brook no passion?

parts.note: lacking passion is being cold
a brook is a small stream

explanation.surface: A regiment that will tolerate no emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brook' looks like the verb to tolerate; it is the noun. The Coldstream Guards are a British Army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coldstream Guards are one of the Foot Guards regiments of the British Army.

clue.text: "They are as sick 'that surfeit with too much, as they that with nothing" (The Merchant of Venice).

definitions.text: "They are as sick 'that surfeit with too much, as they that with nothing" (The Merchant of Venice).

parts.words: "They are as sick 'that surfeit with too much, as they that with nothing" (The Merchant of Venice).
parts.note: a fill-in-the-gap quotation: Nerissa contrasts overeating with going without food

explanation.walkthrough: Nerissa's line in Act 1 Scene 2 has the missing verb between 'they that' and 'with nothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to suffer from having nothing to eat, the opposite of a surfeit.

clue.text: Cleaning up operations in Bath?

parts.note: the city of Bath in England read as a tub, where washing is done

explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English spa city; the capital B disguises the tub.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablutions are the acts of washing oneself.

clue.text: Maiden sound broadcaster.

definitions.meaning: a mythical sea-maiden luring sailors with song
a device emitting a loud warning wail

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the seductive sea nymph of myth and a warning hooter on an ambulance or factory.

clue.text: It's right in advance of the time for crazy demonstrations.

indicators.note: in advance of places the letter for right before the word for the time

parts.note: ages means a long time, as in for ages

explanation.surface: Being right ahead of one's era can lead to wild protests.
explanation.definitionFit: Rages are outbursts of furious anger, crazy displays of temper.

clue.text: The section of a legal opinion that could make one hopping mad?

definitions.text: that could make one hopping mad

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a lawyer's advice that would infuriate a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hopping mad' suggests fury; it is a lively dance with hops.
explanation.definitionFit: A galop is a fast 19th-century ballroom dance full of hopping steps.

clue.text: Composer whose variations were a bit enigmatic.

definitions.text: Composer whose variations were a bit enigmatic.

parts.words: Composer whose variations were a bit enigmatic.
parts.note: points to the English composer of the Enigma Variations

explanation.walkthrough: The Enigma Variations (1899) is the famous orchestral work by this English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar wrote the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: A big laird, in a way, this Italian statesman.

indicators.note: in a way suggests the letters arranged in a different manner

explanation.surface: A Scottish landowner who, in some sense, resembles an Italian leader.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi was a leader of Italian unification.

clue.text: "One equal — of heroic hearts, Made weak by time and fate" (Tennyson).

definitions.text: "One equal — of heroic hearts, Made weak by time and fate" (Tennyson).

parts.words: "One equal — of heroic hearts, Made weak by time and fate" (Tennyson).
parts.note: a fill-in-the-gap quotation from Tennyson's poem Ulysses

explanation.walkthrough: The missing word comes from Ulysses: 'One equal ... of heroic hearts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Temper here means temperament or disposition, the mettle of the heroes.

clue.text: Provide support for a substandard fixture?

parts.note: under means below par, substandard
a pin is a fixing, something that fastens

explanation.definitionFit: To underpin is to support a structure from beneath.
